key_insight: BenchX shows that cancer-detection AI can look strong on average yet fail badly in rare patient subgroups and imaging protocols.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights the need to test tumor-detection models by demographic group, tumor size, and scan protocol before using them in diverse clinical settings.
method: Built an open benchmark of 85,355 CT scans.
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection AI models across tumor size, location, patient subgroup, and imaging protocol.
Used LLMs to extract and organize subgroup information from clinical data.
evidence_signal: The benchmark systematically compared 12 models on 85,355 CT scans and found performance drops in underrepresented subgroups, including young female African Americans.
watch_item: Subgroup labels derived with LLM assistance may require careful validation, and rare groups still have limited data for reliable model training and evaluation.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
